title: Example 17-8: Crossed-Out Letters in Word List

illustrates.quote: When listed or displayed words relating to spelling or word structure are shown with crossed-out letters: a. Transcribe words with crossed-out letters in uncontracted braille. b. Show the word as spelled, without indicating the crossed-out letters. c. Then repeat the word, substituting a hyphen - (36) for each crossed-out letter. d. Explain the use of the hyphen in a transcriber's note.

blocks.text: Words with crossed-out letters are uncontracted, then repeated with a hyphen substituted for each crossed-out letter.

print.notes: Four words, each with one letter ('a') crossed out with a diagonal stroke in print; a standalone transcriber's note (17.11.1d) precedes the list explaining the hyphen convention.
print.printFeatures: A vertical list of four words with a single crossed-out letter each.

braille.notes: Byte-identical between A and B; matches independent re-extraction exactly.

resolution: Both runs (A, B) came from the same model (Gemini Pro via Antigravity, 17 Sep 2026) and are not independent; agreement was treated as no evidence. braille.lines independently re-extracted from references/_text/braille-formats-2016.txt (the line-number field, digits + >=3 spaces, or the fixed left margin measured in ASCII spaces before any U+2800 cell, stripped by counting; U+2800->space; trailing spaces removed). Braille and rule id unchanged (both agreed '17.11.1', matches source). Modeled as a standalone 'note' block (the TN precedes the list, so the generic block-level formatTranscriberNote applies — standards-map.md BANA 17.11.1d 'done') followed by a 'list' block, each item giving both the plain-spelled uncontracted form (17.11.1b) and the hyphen-substituted uncontracted form (17.11.1c); expect MATCH.
